chapter: Bird's world, singers and the new music
title: 'Deep in the Heart of Texas' for June Richmond
summary: In Austin, McGhee writes the arrangement in a day for June Richmond with Kirk's band.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What kinds of things did you sing with Andy's band?
"Deep in The Heart of Texas"? Or was that June Richmond?
That was June Richmond that had it. I wrote the arrangement for it.
I knew you had done something with it.

Yeah. Well, see, we pulled up in Austin, Texas, and we were supposed to play for the university there. And the guy walked up to the bus and told Andy, "If you don't play 'Deep In The Heart Of Texas' I don't think they're going to like you down here." So Andy said, "Look, Maggie, we've got to get this tune. I've been trying to tell you about this tune; we've got to play it tonight." I said, "Oh, damn, man, I don't even know it." He said, "Well, I'll tell you what. I'll give you money and you go down to the music store and see if you can find it, and if you can, write it up for the band tonight." So I says, "Okay."
So I went downtown and got the sheet music to it, and

came back. And I had to stop and figure out, "Now, what am I going to do with it, now that I've got the music. How are we going to play this thing?" You know, I just said, "Oh well, let's let June Richmond do this thing, and then we don't have to have no worries, because she can always break up a house with it." So I wrote the tune, and I asked to find out what key she wanted it in, and so forth and so on. So I wrote it up for her, and we rehearsed it... The first number when we got into the ballroom that night, I said, "Run this down, Andy, so you get an idea what's happening." So he said "Okay," and he kicked it off and we played it down.

So about the middle of the night, the guy wanted to hear "Deep In The Heart Of Texas" and everybody started hollering "Deep in The Heart of Texas'!" So Andy pulled out the arrangement, and said, "Let's lay into it, fellows; let's see what we're going to do with it." And June... I told June, "Come in on the second chorus. You've got the second chorus." So she said, "Okay." So we lit into it, and when she got through singing it, boy, she broke up the goddamn house, and that arrangement, man, led... Well, I don't know whether we recorded it or not; I think we did, but I don't think they released it or something. Because it was just one of those fly-by-night tunes that didn't last
too long, but it was hot...
When it was hot, it was hot, yeah. So that's what happened with June and "Deep In The Heart of Texas."
